trials.label: r1c1
trials.name: reference hedged net
trials.hypothesis: The world-2 reference net unchanged: mask inputs and output maps under 4 layouts (as is, transpose, y-flip, x-flip), summed. If this world deviates the way world 2 did (wrong action layout), it should score about 0.2. A 0 here while a wider hedge scores above 0 means the deviation lies outside these 4 layouts. A 0 everywhere means the deviation is something other than the action layout.

trials.label: r1c2
trials.name: 16-layout symmetry hedge
trials.hypothesis: Hedges all 8 grid symmetries × type-major or type-minor action order, applied both when reading the mask and when laying out the output maps. Rotations and type-minor order are deviations that the 4-layout reference cannot represent. This should score above 0 if the action layout is one of these 16. If it scores 0 while the reference scores above 0, the extra layouts cost too much learning signal. If both score 0, the action layout is probably not the deviation.

trials.label: r1c3
trials.name: reference with 5x5 head
trials.hypothesis: The reference net with a 5x5 head conv (width 24, to keep r near 1.2), which hedges against anchors that aren't top-left (centre or bottom-right) and against footprints larger than described. Each placement logit then sees 5x5 around its anchor before the trunk adds context. This should beat the reference if anchors or footprints deviate. It is refuted if it scores no better than the reference.

trials.label: r1c4
trials.name: DONE-index hedge
trials.hypothesis: Adds a hedge on where DONE sits: at the last index, or at index 0 with all placements shifted by one. Each position has its own mask reading, its own maps under the 4 reference layouts and its own DONE logit, all summed. If DONE is really at index 0, every non-hedged net mis-places by one cell and also ends episodes by accident, so this net alone should score above 0. It is refuted if it ties the reference.

trials.label: r1c5
trials.name: max hedge: 16 layouts x DONE
trials.hypothesis: Combines the 16 action layouts with both DONE positions: 32 mask readings in, and 32 summed output maps plus DONE logits out. This covers any combination of grid symmetry, type order and DONE index. It should be the only candidate above 0 if the world combines two of these deviations. It is refuted if it scores 0 while a narrower hedge succeeds, which would mean the extra hedging dilutes learning.

trials.label: r1c6
trials.name: max hedge + 5x5 + mask skip
trials.hypothesis: The maximum hedge plus a 5x5 head conv (width 24) for other anchors and footprints. The laid-out mask also feeds the head's 1x1 skip directly, so per-action legality, which reveals heights near the top and the true action layout, reaches the logits without passing through the trunk. This targets combined layout, anchor and dynamics deviations. It is refuted if it scores no better than the plain maximum hedge.

trials.label: r2c1
trials.name: adaptive 24-layout hedge
trials.hypothesis: Two changes from the reference. First, an adaptive action space: if n_place is a multiple of YX it uses K=n_place/(YX) maps, which covers actions that include z or rotations; it also handles the compact per-footprint anchor layout. Second, 24 layouts, adding type-middle orders (Y,T,X) and (X,T,Y) to the 16 already tried. Should score above 0 if the action layout or count is the deviation. It is refuted if it scores 0.

trials.label: r2c2
trials.name: adaptive + dense permutation path
trials.hypothesis: Adaptive action space with 4 layouts, plus a dense layout-free path at full scale. The full mask goes through a Linear into 4 grid channels, and the flattened head features go through a Linear to all action logits; both are summed with the spatial logits. This targets an arbitrary fixed permutation of action indices, which no symmetry hedge can represent. The spatial path still trains at once. It is refuted if it scores 0 like the round-1 nets.

trials.label: r2c3
trials.name: adaptive + separate critic
trials.hypothesis: Adaptive action space with 4 layouts. The critic gets its own small conv pathway (1x1 to 32, 3x3, pooled MLP), so the value loss no longer shapes the policy trunk. This targets a reward scale that differs from the description, where a large value loss would swamp the policy features in a shared trunk. It is refuted if it scores 0 like the reference.

trials.label: r2c4
trials.name: adaptive + deep dilated trunk
trials.hypothesis: This is the reference 4-layout hedge on a deeper trunk: four residual 3x3 convs with dilations 1,2,1,2 and global mean/max mixing halfway. It also reads compact action layouts and multiple extra actions automatically, and trains with 1 PPO epoch for more samples. Width is cut from 48 to 40 (cost about 1.5×) so the check run fits 4 or more updates. Targets a deviation that needs long-range context, such as other dynamics or heights. Refuted if it stays at 0 with zero training success.

trials.label: r2c5
trials.name: kitchen-sink hedge
trials.hypothesis: Combines every hedge at once: 24 action layouts (type-major, type-minor and type-middle orders under all 8 symmetries) times 2 DONE positions; the obs also read transposed and channel-last; a dense Linear mask embedding plus a dense logit path; a separate value stem; and a deep dilated trunk. Width is cut to 32, stem to 48 and value stem to 16 (cost about 1.5×) so the check run fits. Refuted if it stays at 0 with zero training success.

trials.label: r2c6
trials.name: adaptive + obs memory-layout hedge
trials.hypothesis: Adaptive action space with 4 layouts. The obs is also re-read as raw (Y,X,C) and (X,Y,C) memory reshaped into [C,Y,X], and all three readings are concatenated before the learned 1x1 stem. This targets an obs whose data is stored channel-last but labelled channel-first. Every round-1 net would then have seen spatially scrambled inputs, which no output-layout hedge can fix. It is refuted if it scores 0.

trials.label: r3c1
trials.name: obs 8-sym + 16 action layouts
trials.hypothesis: The whole obs is concatenated under all 8 grid symmetries before the 1x1 stem, so each channel group (build, target, missing, extra, heights) can be read in its own frame. This targets target or missing channels mirrored or transposed relative to the build, which no earlier trial covered. The 16 action layouts are kept on the mask and output. Refuted if it stays at 0 with 0 training success.

trials.label: r3c2
trials.name: obs 8-sym, lean action hedge
trials.hypothesis: The 8 obs symmetries are also enough to place the obs in the mask/action frame. So only 2 action layouts (identity, type-major or type-minor) are kept, which cuts output dilution compared with candidate 1. Targets a target-vs-build frame mismatch or an obs-vs-action symmetry, with less summed noise. Refuted if it scores 0. If it beats candidate 1, the wide output hedge costs learning signal.

trials.label: r3c3
trials.name: per-group learned cell remaps
trials.hypothesis: Each obs channel group (build, target, missing, extra, heights+time) gets its own learned YX-to-YX Linear cell remap, shared across that group's channels and default-initialised. Each remap sits beside the raw obs at full scale, with no gate. A learned YX-to-YX remap is also added to the output maps. This targets an arbitrary fixed scramble of cells within an obs group, or relative to the actions, which symmetry hedges cannot represent. Refuted if it stays at 0.

trials.label: r3c4
trials.name: cheap obs 8-sym, 1 epoch
trials.hypothesis: The same obs-symmetry hedge with 2 action layouts, on a narrower net (stem 48, width 32, so r is about 1) with 1 PPO epoch. That gives about 420k steps instead of about 200k. If frames are mismatched but the policy needs more samples to escape zero, this should score where candidate 2 does not. Refuted if it scores 0 while candidate 2 scores 0 too, since the sample count would then not be the bottleneck.

trials.label: r3c5
trials.name: obs 8-sym max hedge, 5x5 + mask skip
trials.hypothesis: Obs symmetries combined with 16 action layouts × 2 DONE positions, a 5x5 head conv (other anchors or footprints) and the laid-out mask fed straight into the head skip. Stem 48 and 1 PPO epoch keep the step count near 260k. This targets frame-mismatched obs together with another action or anchor deviation. Refuted if it scores 0 while candidate 1 also scores 0.

trials.label: r3c6
trials.name: sym + remap kitchen sink
trials.hypothesis: Combines both new obs hedges: 8 obs symmetries plus per-group learned cell remaps. Output maps get a learned YX remap, under 16 action layouts × 2 DONE positions. Stem 48 and 1 PPO epoch. This covers any mix of symmetric or scrambled obs frames together with action-layout and DONE deviations. Refuted if it stays at 0. If it scores while candidates 1 and 3 do not, the deviation is a combination.

trials.label: r4c1
trials.name: log-compressed inputs
trials.hypothesis: The reference 4-layout hedge, but each obs channel first passes through its own learned 1x1 (depthwise, 2 outputs per channel) and then a signed log1p. This targets obs values scaled outside [0,1], such as raw heights or a raw step count up to 33, which would swamp a plain stem. Every earlier net fed the raw obs. Refuted if it stays at 0 with zero training success.

trials.label: r4c2
trials.name: footprint-pool + hedge
trials.hypothesis: The reference 4-layout hedge plus a footprint-pooling head, summed at full scale into every layout's maps. For each spec footprint it takes learned features pooled with max, min and mean under both top-left and bottom-right anchors. This targets the bottleneck of learning, under possibly changed drop dynamics, whether every cell under a footprint lands on missing target cells. Neither the pooling start net nor the hedged net had both parts. Refuted if it stays at 0.

trials.label: r4c3
trials.name: 3D layer encoder
trials.hypothesis: Adds a small learned 3D encoder over (build, target, missing, extra) × Z layers, with a 3x3x3 conv to 8 channels and then a 3x1x1 conv along z. Its output, flattened into the 2D stem, sits beside the raw obs at full scale. This gives layer-equivariant features (support below, missing at the landing layer), robust to changed drop or height rules. The 2D stem must learn these separately for each layer. Refuted if it stays at 0.

trials.label: r4c4
trials.name: compress + decoupled critic, long horizon
trials.hypothesis: Log-compressed inputs plus a separate critic whose gradient is scaled by 0.1 (the forward value is unchanged), so a large or sparse reward cannot dominate the global gradient clip. The recipe uses gamma 0.99, lambda 0.95 and entropy 0.01. This targets a reward deviation: little shaping, or a large scale where only the terminal bonus guides learning, which gamma 0.9 cannot credit. Earlier trials used a separate critic only with gamma 0.9. Refuted if it stays at 0.

trials.label: r4c5
trials.name: compress + pool + 3D encoder
trials.hypothesis: Combines the three new representation hedges (log-compressed inputs, footprint-pooling head, 3D layer encoder) on the reference 4-layout hedge with the world-2 recipe, at r about 1.4. If the deviation needs scale robustness and layer-aware footprint reasoning together, only this net should score. Refuted if it stays at 0. If it scores while candidates 1-3 do not, the deviation is a combination.

trials.label: r4c6
trials.name: all-new hedges, 16 layouts, 1 epoch
trials.hypothesis: The maximum combination: log-compressed inputs, footprint pooling and the 3D layer encoder. It keeps the 16 action layouts (8 symmetries × type order) and adds a separate critic with its gradient scaled by 0.1. It trains 1 PPO epoch to keep the sample count near 250k despite r of about 1.6. This covers a new representation deviation combined with an action-layout deviation. Refuted if it stays at 0.

analyses.1: There are no results in this world yet. The starting net scored 0, and the starting net also scored 0 in world 2, where only the reference net with layout hedging succeeded (~0.22). Earlier evidence suggests zeros come from deviations the world doesn't describe, not from the recipe or capacity. So round 1 bets only on what the network assumes, and every candidate keeps the reference recipe. Without data, nothing is ruled out yet. One assumption is safe: the 1x1 stem mixes all obs channels freely, so a permuted channel order cannot by itself cause failure. A transposed or flipped obs relative to the actions is covered by hedging the output layout, because only the relative alignment matters. The candidates are: the reference; the full set of 16 action layouts (8 grid symmetries × type-major or type-minor); a 5x5 head conv for other footprints and anchors; DONE at index 0 or at the end; and two combined maximum hedges. Each file falls back to a Linear mask embedding if n_place ≠ T·Y·X.
analyses.2: All six round-1 nets scored 0 on dev and in training. Ruled out, at the reference recipe: the 16 symmetry × type-order layouts, DONE at index 0, anchor offsets of 1 to 2 cells and footprints up to 5x5. Obs channel order cannot be the cause, because the learned 1x1 stem gives the same result under any channel permutation. What remains open: (1) n_place ≠ n_types·Y·X. Every round-1 file then fell back to the same slow dense Linear head, which would explain a uniform 0. (2) Type-middle action orders (Y,T,X). (3) An arbitrary action permutation. (4) An obs whose memory layout is scrambled (stored as Y,X,C but labelled C,Y,X). (5) A reward scale whose value loss swamps the shared trunk. (6) Harder dynamics that need more receptive field or more samples. Every candidate now adapts its action layout to the spec: K=n_place/(YX) maps, a compact per-footprint anchor layout, or the dense fallback. On top of that, each tests one further bet, and one candidate combines all of them.
analyses.3: Twelve trials, and every one scored 0 on dev and 0 in training. That rules out these deviations: the 24 action layouts (8 grid symmetries times type-major, type-minor and type-middle order), DONE at index 0, the compact per-footprint action layout and a multiple-of-YX action count, a fixed scramble of action indices (dense path), the obs stored channel-last, other anchors or footprints (5x5 head), reward scale (separate critic) and short context (dilated trunk). Obs channel order is already hedged, because the first 1x1 conv mixes all channels. All the hedges so far kept the obs internally consistent, so obs parts that disagree with each other remain untested. If the target and build channels sit in different frames, the net would need a global transform that local convs cannot learn. This round adds two such hedges: all 8 symmetries of the whole obs fed to the 1x1 stem, and learned cell remaps for each channel group. If these also score 0, the deviation is probably reward or dynamics, which the network cannot fix.
analyses.4: All 18 trials scored exactly 0 on dev and in training. None of these moved the score: 24 action layouts, both DONE positions, 8 obs symmetries, a channel-last obs, learned cell remaps, a 5x5 head, a dense permutation path, a separate critic, a deeper trunk, or 1 epoch with 426k steps. The 1x1 stem can already learn any obs channel permutation, z-order or group swap, so those are ruled out in practice. What remains untested is how inputs and features are represented. Obs values may lie outside [0,1], for example raw heights or a raw step count. The net may lack layer-aware 3D features or footprint statistics for working out where a brick lands under changed dynamics. The reward may be sparse, which needs a longer horizon and a critic that cannot take over the gradient. This is the last round, so each candidate pairs the reference hedge with one of these untested ideas, plus two combinations, so that any nonzero score has the best chance.
